status: exact first signed correction for the critical Dirichlet blocks with a guarded second-order remainder programme
proof_boundary: This artifact proves the shifted-ratio identity, Gaussian moment, first correction formula, and logarithmic remainder decomposition. It does not certify the uniform C_D/T^2 remainder, the resulting global exp(-5L/4) C^1 constants, the cutoff collar, the strict signed contact inequality, contact exclusion, Lambda<=0, or RH.

exact.central_tail_split: Split |v|<=V and |v|>V with V=T^(1/3), T=Im(s): use the second-order expansions on the central part and the published Proposition 6.1 quadratic Gaussian envelope on the tail
exact.per_term_target: |r_(t,n)/m_(t,n)-(1+d_(t,n))|<=C_D/T^2 uniformly for n<=N on the critical radius-1/L collar
exact.finite_sum_scale: sum of the two absolute finite-main coefficient masses <=50*exp(L/4), T>=2*pi*exp(L-1)
exact.global_scale_handoff: The peeled Dirichlet residual is O(exp(-7L/4)); the RS-C_1 endpoint and cutoff residuals are O(exp(-5L/4)) and therefore set the next global C^1 scale
exact.uniform_target: Prove explicit constants eta_0,eta_1 with |r_[1]|<=eta_0*exp(-5L/4), |r_[1],x|<=eta_1*L*exp(-5L/4) on L>=50, 0<tL<=25, including adjacent cutoffs, then use r_0=DeltaJ in the signed contact-normal inequality

rows.claim: Polymath 15 gives an exact contour-shifted Gaussian formula for every evolved Dirichlet block.
rows.proof_boundary: Equation (40), with its stated contour condition.

rows.claim: The exact gamma prefactor is the Polymath normalizer times the standard scaled gamma function.
rows.proof_boundary: Algebraic comparison of the exact xi gamma factor with M_0; DLMF supplies the signed scaled-gamma expansion.

rows.claim: After the saddle shift, every discarded finite-sum factor is contained in one exact centered Gaussian expectation.
rows.proof_boundary: No asymptotic truncation in the displayed ratio.

rows.claim: The shifted Gaussian second moment is explicit.
rows.proof_boundary: Uses integral v dmu=0 and integral v^2 dmu=1/2.

rows.claim: The complete first signed relative correction combines the scaled-gamma term with the quadratic log-M_0 term.
rows.proof_boundary: Exact coefficient extraction; the size of the remainder after truncation is a separate obligation.

rows.claim: The unretained logarithmic error splits into an explicit M_0 Taylor remainder, scaled-gamma remainder, and rational shift difference.
rows.proof_boundary: Exact Taylor remainder identity on the chosen branch.

rows.claim: A published complex-sector log-gamma remainder reduces to an integrable upper-half-plane bound.
rows.proof_boundary: The DLMF bound is published; its uniform insertion into the full heat collar still needs explicit branch and denominator bookkeeping.

rows.claim: A central/tail split prevents the cubic Taylor remainder from being exponentiated on the entire Gaussian line.
rows.formula: Split |v|<=V and |v|>V with V=T^(1/3), T=Im(s): use the second-order expansions on the central part and the published Proposition 6.1 quadratic Gaussian envelope on the tail; |r_(t,n)/m_(t,n)-(1+d_(t,n))|<=C_D/T^2 uniformly for n<=N on the critical radius-1/L collar; sum of the two absolute finite-main coefficient masses <=50*exp(L/4), T>=2*pi*exp(L-1); C_D/T^2 times 50*exp(L/4)=O(C_D*exp(-7L/4))
rows.proof_boundary: Architecture only. The finite constant C_D and collar monotonicity inequalities are not certified here.

rows.claim: The two Dirichlet corrections and the endpoint correction combine into the signed remainder model required at contact.
rows.formula: DeltaJ=(DeltaA+DeltaB-DeltaC)/A_t, J_[1]=J_[0]+DeltaJ, r_[0]=DeltaJ+r_[1]; The peeled Dirichlet residual is O(exp(-7L/4)); the RS-C_1 endpoint and cutoff residuals are O(exp(-5L/4)) and therefore set the next global C^1 scale
rows.proof_boundary: Exact repartition once DeltaA, DeltaB, and DeltaC are defined; the claimed scale remains conditional on the open bounds.

rows.claim: The first-order asymptotic programme reduces to one explicit global second-order value/first-jet estimate.
rows.formula: Prove explicit constants eta_0,eta_1 with |r_[1]|<=eta_0*exp(-5L/4), |r_[1],x|<=eta_1*L*exp(-5L/4) on L>=50, 0<tL<=25, including adjacent cutoffs, then use r_0=DeltaJ in the signed contact-normal inequality
rows.proof_boundary: Open. No strict signed contact inequality, contact exclusion, Lambda<=0, or RH is asserted.
